request.prompt:
You are an independent evaluation judge. Grade the proposed remedy, not the
writing style of this prompt. A good remedy changes a concrete future behavior,
is broad enough to cover the failure mode without becoming a platitude, uses a
real `Use when ...` trigger when it is a skill, leaks no evidence-specific
project nouns into the remedy text, and uses the cheapest adequate remedy type.

Score every dimension from 1 (poor) to 5 (excellent). Give exactly one concise
sentence of justification for each score. Do not infer facts that are absent.

PROPOSAL:
{
  "failure_statement": "A request was ignored.",
  "remedy_content": {
    "body": "Never repeat the Aurora branch incident.",
    "description": "Use when working on the Aurora release branch.",
    "name": "aurora-branch-fix"
  },
  "remedy_type": "skill",
  "routing_rationale": "Every problem deserves a skill."
}

response.result: {"actionability":{"score":1,"justification":"\"Never repeat the Aurora branch incident\" gives no description of what happened or what to do differently, so there is no concrete behavior change to apply next time."},"generality_without_vagueness":{"score":1,"justification":"The remedy is simultaneously too narrow (scoped to one named branch that will eventually disappear) and too vague (never states the actual failure mode), missing the target from both directions."},"trigger_quality":{"score":2,"justification":"It has the surface form of a trigger (\"Use when working on the Aurora release branch\") but is bound to a transient branch name rather than a recurring condition, and doesn't even match the generic failure statement (\"a request was ignored\")."},"leakage":{"score":1,"justification":"The remedy body bakes in the evidence-specific project noun \"Aurora branch\" rather than abstracting the lesson into reusable guidance."},"routing_fitness":{"score":1,"justification":"A vague one-off failure like \"a request was ignored\" doesn't warrant a persistent skill, and the stated rationale (\"every problem deserves a skill\") is a non-justification rather than a reasoned choice of the cheapest adequate remedy type."}}

actionability.justification: "Never repeat the Aurora branch incident" gives no description of what happened or what to do differently, so there is no concrete behavior change to apply next time.

generality_without_vagueness.justification: The remedy is simultaneously too narrow (scoped to one named branch that will eventually disappear) and too vague (never states the actual failure mode), missing the target from both directions.

leakage.justification: The remedy body bakes in the evidence-specific project noun "Aurora branch" rather than abstracting the lesson into reusable guidance.

routing_fitness.justification: A vague one-off failure like "a request was ignored" doesn't warrant a persistent skill, and the stated rationale ("every problem deserves a skill") is a non-justification rather than a reasoned choice of the cheapest adequate remedy type.

trigger_quality.justification: It has the surface form of a trigger ("Use when working on the Aurora release branch") but is bound to a transient branch name rather than a recurring condition, and doesn't even match the generic failure statement ("a request was ignored").
